messages:
Nina: kicking off prep for Helix QBR — main ask from account team is a clear spend forecast and actions to avoid a mid-quarter renewal surprise. can we get a 30/60/90 view + top 3 mitigations?
Evan: I pulled last 30d token burn — trending +18% mo, mostly from embeddings (indexing job). forecast model shows potential 45% overcommit by month end if growth continues.
Sam: embedding jobs are running unbatched in their integration. sent a patch to reduce batch frequency earlier this week, but it hasn’t been deployed to production on their side. cc @Ivy for onboarding status.
Ivy: helix onboarding still has two remaining tasks: (1) switch to batched embedding endpoint, (2) enable prefix KV cache for chat session. both are on their engineer backlog, ETA 7 business days.
Nina: ok — for QBR we should present: 1) forecast (baseline/optimistic/pessimistic), 2) immediate guardrails (alerts, throttles), 3) enablement asks. Evan can you draft the forecast numbers? Sam, can you prepare the minimal code snippet to enable batching?
Evan: Draft numbers: baseline = current trajectory -> $12.4k/mo, optimistic (after batching & cache) -> $7.1k/mo, pessimistic (no changes + growth) -> $18.0k/mo. assumptions: 30% reduction from batching, 20% from KV caching, 12% monthly usage growth. I’ll attach a one-slide chart.
Sam: snippet for their engineers (copy/paste):
```
# python pseudo
from redwood_sdk import EmbeddingsClient
client = EmbeddingsClient()
client.create_batch_job(inputs=batch_inputs, batch_size=64, flush_interval_seconds=5)
```
Sam: also add note to enable async batching on their worker process — that gives immediate ~25-35% savings on our benchmarks.
Ivy: onboarding status note for QBR: "Customer aware of plan, engineering bandwidth limited, CS to own follow-up and provide a 2hr enablement session next week."
Nina: alerts — can we set a temporary budget throttle and an email + slack alert at 60/80/95% of committed monthly spend? redwood-billing-bot, can you confirm capability?
redwood-billing-bot: yes — created alerts for account helix: thresholds=[60,80,95], notify_channels=[#cs-helix,#finance], action=notify. Budget throttle requires manual opt-in by account admin.
Evan: recommend also proposing a short reserved capacity trial (1 week) for their peak ETL job to smooth unit economics — we can show comparison in QBR.
Nina: great. action items: @Sam prepare code + 1-pager by EOD Thu, @Evan attach slide with forecast + reserved trial ROI, @Ivy schedule 2hr enablement session and confirm attendee list, I’ll own the QBR narrative and next steps.
Sam: ack. will include quick test harness and benchmark numbers.
Evan: ack. putting numbers into the slide now.
Ivy: scheduling meeting — sending calendar invites today.
Nina: final QBR bullets for thread (for notes): "Spend spike root cause = unbatched embedding ingestion; near-term mitigations = batching + KV cache + throttle alerts; medium-term = reserved capacity trial + engineering cleanup; CS enablement = 2hr workshop + code drop."
Sam: adding sample CI test to validate batching (will paste into the doc).
Nina: thanks team — I’ll send the draft QBR deck once Evan’s slide is in. :thumbsup:
